visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 consistently shows the correct gas container, thermometer, volume/amount labels, pressure target, and correct PV=nRT rearrangement/substitution, while Lesson 2 has a visibly broken/incomplete calculation frame and a confusing final container label that appears to use the wrong unit/meaning despite reaching the right numeric answer.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired quiz gate after act_setup with a real question, plausible options, and a correct answer, whereas Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, natural narration with correctly spoken math and appropriate pacing, while Lesson 2 has no transcript/narration available to evaluate, making it worse on narration quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides timed cues that generally coincide with the referenced narration, whereas Lesson 2 has no transcript or cue timing available at all, making its visual-narration sync absent and unevaluable.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly applies and explains the ideal gas law step by step, including isolating P, substituting values, units, and arithmetic, while Lesson 2 has no available transcript or content to verify any conceptual accuracy or pedagogical explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 is simpler but generally legible, centered, and uncluttered, whereas Lesson 1 has persistent tiny/clipped top text, off-frame/cropped elements, and increasingly crowded panels that hurt presentation polish.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: five of six agents preferred it, all with very high confidence, across the most substantive dimensions—visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy. These agents found that Lesson 1 correctly presents and explains the ideal gas law, includes functioning interactivity, has clear narration, and aligns visuals with narration. Lesson 2 only won polish, with lower confidence, because it appeared cleaner and less cluttered, but this was outweighed by missing or incomplete narration, sync, interactivity, and verifiable instructional content.
